title: Root '.' component uses an exact file list, not a glob
context: deriveComponents (src/extractors/indexer.ts) synthesized a directory-level component named "." with paths: ["./**"] whenever a repo has any indexed file directly at its root (no subdirectory). pathMatchesGlob (src/core/glob.ts) normalizes away a leading "./", so "./**" compiled to /^.*$/ and matched EVERY file in the repo — every symbol in the repo got attributed to the "." component. Independently, wiki.ts's owns() (assemblePack's ownership check) rejected the "./" prefix outright and matched NOTHING for the same paths, so the two matchers disagreed about what "." meant. Surfaced by issue #22 (YAML language support), since a root-level socket.yml was the first root-level file this repo ever indexed — but the bug is generic, not YAML-specific: it fires for any repo with a root-level indexed file of any language. Tracked as issue #34, fixed in PR #37.
decision: For the root group (dir === "."), deriveComponents now lists the actual root-level file paths exactly (e.g. ["config.ts", "settings.ts"]) instead of synthesizing any glob. Root-level file sets are small and static, so an exact list is a natural fit. Both pathMatchesGlob's exact-match fast path (g === p) and owns()'s prefix/exact check already handle a glob-char-free path correctly with zero changes to glob.ts or wiki.ts — so the fix is confined to the one producer (deriveComponents) instead of touching either shared matcher.
consequences: The "." component's ownership is now asymmetric versus directory components: it only covers root files that carried symbols at the LAST index — a new root-level file isn't owned until the next `hunch index` — whereas a directory component's glob (e.g. src/foo/**) matches anything under that directory whether or not it was indexed at glob-authoring time.
Any repo with a previously-committed "./**" root component self-heals on the next `hunch index` with no migration needed, since paths is always freshly derived from the current scan.

Filed issue #38 to track the underlying systemic risk as separate follow-up: at least three independent interpretations of component.paths exist in the tree (pathMatchesGlob, owns()/globPrefix, delivery.ts's anchor path, plus evaluator.ts's own glob-detection regex) that happen to agree today by construction but aren't contractually tied together.
alternatives_rejected: Keep emitting "./**": the original bug. pathMatchesGlob normalizes away the leading "./", so globToRegExp("**") compiles to /^.*$/ and matches every file in the repo, not just root-level ones.

Emit "*" instead of "./**": pathMatchesGlob handles "*" correctly (matches root files only, via /^[^/]*$/). But globPrefix("*") computes to "", and wiki.ts's owns() deliberately skips empty prefixes as a guard against a repo-wide glob owning everything on a component page — so the wiki would again own NOTHING for the "." component. Same failure mode as "./**", from the opposite direction.

Fix pathMatchesGlob/globToRegExp globally to preserve leading "./" semantics (so "./**" genuinely means root-level-only): correct in principle, but pathMatchesGlob is the shared matcher for every constraint/policy scope in the graph (consumed by src/eval/guards.ts, src/constitution/evaluator.ts, src/core/delivery.ts, src/store/hunchStore.ts, src/synthesis/synthesize.ts, src/constitution/composition.ts, src/constitution/sourceMutation.ts, src/constitution/structural.ts). Changing its semantics for a "./"-prefixed-glob case that is otherwise unused elsewhere in the graph is a much larger blast radius than fixing the one producer that emits it.

Suppress creating a "." component altogether, leaving root-level files uncomponentized: simplest option, and matches how loose top-level config files are often treated as not belonging to any subsystem. Rejected because it throws away real information (which root files exist, hunch_structure visibility) for no strong reason — the issue's own text treats this as the fallback, not the preferred fix.
